pages.text: A porphyry copper stock carries chalcopyrite with a little molybdenite, and the molybdenite carries rhenium at parts per million. A copper sulfide smelts not to copper but to matte. Chalcopyrite roasted on a fire, or the calcine bornite, chalcocite and covellite roast to, melts in the bloomery to copper matte and slag.
pages.title: The porphyry chain

pages.text: Two matte and a sand, superheated, are the converter: the air burns off the sulfur and the iron, which the sand fluxes to slag, and leaves two blister copper. The blast furnace fire-refines blister to copper.
Two raw molybdenite roasted in a heated basin give two molybdenum trioxide, and half the time a rhenium flue dust: the roaster's flue is where every gram of the world's rhenium comes from.

Both oxides are reduced under hydrogen in a heated chemical vat with an industrial mixer, as the industry does: two trioxide and 500 mB of hydrogen give two molybdenum ingots, two flue dust and 250 mB give one rhenium ingot. Hydrogen is The Factory Must Grow's.
